nodes.label: Mira Web Platform
nodes.rationale: New web platform for Mira replacing the old site. NOT an e-commerce and does not sell products; the primary goal is to generate quote requests (orcamento). Target audience: food service, bakery, confectionery and ice-cream businesses who want to find products quickly, so every UX decision prioritizes simplicity and speed.

nodes.label: Tech Stack (Next.js 15 / React 19 / Prisma / PostgreSQL)
nodes.rationale: Next.js 15 + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + Lucide; backend via Route Handlers and Server Actions; PostgreSQL + Prisma; Auth.js; Resend for email; deploy via Docker on an Ubuntu VPS behind Nginx. Server Components preferred, Client Components only when necessary.

nodes.label: Feature-based Architecture (Zod → Server Action → Service)
nodes.rationale: Each entity is organized as features/<entity>/{schemas,services,actions,components} with pages under app. Mandatory flow: Zod validates → Server Action (validate, call service, revalidatePath, redirect) → Service (Prisma). No database logic in components or actions; no business logic in components. Enforces SOLID/DRY/KISS and easy maintenance.

nodes.label: Public Quote Flow
nodes.rationale: The heart of the site: Product → add to quote → Minha Cotacao → fill name/CPF-CNPJ/email/phone/company/notes → send → save to DB + email commercial team. CPF/CNPJ validated by check digit; client confirmation email sent; protocol format ORC-000123. Server is the source of truth — client-supplied name/image never trusted.

nodes.label: Quote Cart (client localStorage store)
nodes.rationale: Context + Provider persisting to localStorage (key mira:quote-cart). Hydration flag avoids SSR/CSR mismatch; syncs across tabs via storage event; discards corrupt data. Supports multiple lines per product keyed by productId + flavorId (rewritten to support flavors).

nodes.label: Quote / QuoteItem models
nodes.rationale: createQuote runs in a $transaction: revalidates products (only ACTIVE), atomic protocol via upsert ON CONFLICT on Settings.quote_sequence (no race, no migration). QuoteItem uses onDelete Restrict to Product to preserve history; snapshots flavor + unit; unique changed to [quoteId, productId, flavor] so a product can have multiple lines (one per flavor).

nodes.label: Product
nodes.rationale: Catalog entity with no price field (the site only quotes, never sells). Has saleUnit (default 'unidade'), flavors, optional nutrition, categoryId (always the root/main category) and optional subcategoryId. SKU unique; slug auto-generated. Search matches name OR SKU (case-insensitive contains).

nodes.label: Category with 2-level Subcategories
nodes.rationale: Two-level hierarchy (category → subcategory) via the pre-existing parent/children self-relation — no migration needed. The two-level invariant is enforced in the service (assertValidParent), not the DB: a parent must be a root, a category with children cannot become a subcategory. Subcategory modeled as its own product field (subcategoryId) so categoryId is always the main category; managed embedded in the category edit screen.

nodes.label: Supplier (renamed from Brand)
nodes.rationale: Client-facing label 'Fornecedores'. Structural rename Brand → Supplier done via Prisma @@map("Brand") so the physical table stays Brand — zero DB drift, no destructive migration (a real table rename would be drop+create and lose data). Identifiers in English, routes/UI in Portuguese (/fornecedores).

nodes.label: ProductFlavor
nodes.rationale: A product can have flavors, each with its own photo; a customer can order several flavors of the same product with per-flavor quantity. onDelete Cascade. Shown publicly as a horizontal carousel; each flavor can have its own nutrition table that overrides the product-level general table.

nodes.label: Nutrition Tables (ANVISA) per Product/Flavor
nodes.rationale: Brazilian nutrition table (ANVISA RDC 429/2020 + IN 75/2020) built in HTML/React/Tailwind, not an image. Official on-package values stored as-is — never recalculated (IN 75/2020 rounding is complex). Nutrition is optional. NutritionFacts belongs to exactly one owner — a product (general table) OR a flavor (per-flavor override); public display falls back to the general table when the selected flavor has none.

nodes.label: Admin Panel
nodes.rationale: Simple, intuitive panel with menus: Dashboard, Produtos, Categorias, Fornecedores, Cotacoes, Usuarios, Configuracoes. Scoped CMS: only the catalog and site Settings are editable; institutional pages live in code (no generic CMS). Nav filtered by role (Usuarios and Configuracoes are ADMIN-only).

nodes.label: Authentication (Auth.js edge-split)
nodes.rationale: Config split for Edge compatibility: lib/auth.config.ts is edge-safe (no Prisma/bcrypt, providers:[]) and used by middleware; lib/auth.ts is Node runtime and adds the real Credentials provider. Defense in depth: middleware protects /admin/*, layouts and pages re-check session, and mutating actions guard via guardAdminWrite. Login moved to /login. getCurrentUser reads role fresh from DB (role not put in JWT).

nodes.label: Rate Limiting (in-memory fixed window)
nodes.rationale: In-memory fixed-window limiter chosen deliberately for the target deploy (single Docker/Node process on one VPS); counter resets on redeploy and is not shared across replicas — swap the store for a shared backend if scaling horizontally. Login: 5 failures/60s per IP (only failures count). Admin writes: 40 ops/60s per IP. Quote submit: 5 sends/10min per IP.

nodes.label: Local Image Uploads (VPS storage)
nodes.rationale: 100% local storage on the server — Cloudinary removed, no third parties, no manual URLs, no image in the DB (only the path). Writes to public/uploads/<folder>/<uuid>.<ext>; extension derived from MIME not the uploaded name; route validates auth + folder allowlist (anti-traversal) + format + size (raised 5MB → 20MB). cleanup deletes orphan files only when no record references them. public/uploads must be a persistent Docker volume.

nodes.label: Site Settings
nodes.rationale: Key-value Settings editable in the panel — scope reduced to contact, social networks and quote email recipients (8 keys). Site name/description/hero moved to code (SITE_CONFIG). getSiteSettings uses unstable_cache (tag site-settings); saving calls revalidateTag so footer/hero/WhatsApp refresh immediately. Settings.quote_sequence also backs the atomic quote protocol counter.

nodes.label: SEO (Metadata API, sitemap, Schema.org)
nodes.rationale: Metadata API, Open Graph, robots.txt, sitemap.xml, Schema.org and canonical URLs. Product SEO is automatic: generateMetadata uses metaTitle ?? name and metaDescription ?? summary derived from the description; legacy meta fields kept but no longer written from the panel.

nodes.label: Prisma 7 Driver Adapter decision
nodes.rationale: In Prisma 7 the datasource block no longer accepts url; prisma.config.ts only supplies the connection URL to the CLI. Any runtime PrismaClient requires an explicit driver adapter, so @prisma/adapter-pg + pg are dependencies and every client is instantiated as new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg({ connectionString }) }) — never bare new PrismaClient(). Migrations generated via migrate diff --from-config-datasource (Prisma 7 dropped --from-url).

nodes.label: Resend Quote Emails (graceful degradation)
nodes.rationale: Sends two emails (commercial + client confirmation). sendQuoteEmails NEVER throws: without RESEND_API_KEY/RESEND_FROM_EMAIL or on error, the quote is already saved and the failure is logged — the request is never lost. Recipient from Settings → fallback env. Emails include a Codigo (SKU) column. env validation accepts either a plain email or 'Name <email>' format for RESEND_FROM_EMAIL.

nodes.label: Suppliers & Segments shown even without products
nodes.rationale: Client decision: a newly registered supplier or category/segment should appear on the site immediately without needing a linked product. Removed the _count.products > 0 filter from the home supplier carousel, the products-page supplier section, and 'Compre por segmento'. Trade-off accepted: clicking a productless supplier/segment lands on an empty listing until products are added; active:false still hides them.

nodes.label: Global Search (header autocomplete)
nodes.rationale: Single textual-search entry point — the header magnifier with real-time suggestions (products by name/SKU, categories, suppliers). GET /api/search (read-only, consistent with the catalog) with debounce + AbortController. Shared search constants live in a Prisma-free module: importing a value from a module that pulls lib/prisma into a client component breaks the build with 'Can't resolve fs'.

nodes.label: Public Site Layout & Hero
nodes.rationale: Public layout: single-bar header (utility strip removed) that is transparent over the hero and turns solid on scroll, with white↔colored logo swap; full-screen home hero slider (6 slides, gradient fallback until photos exist); dark footer; WhatsApp float. Institutional pages (Quem Somos, Nossas Unidades) are static in code.

nodes.label: Brand Visual Identity
nodes.rationale: Palette applied via CSS tokens: --primary blue #17479e (buttons, links, active nav, focus ring) and --brand red #ed1c24 (conversion CTAs). Fonts Public Sans (body) + Archivo (display). Standardized to only these two brand colors + shades. Dark mode tokens exist but dark mode is not activated (client wants to refine both themes first; needs logo-mira-dark.png + next-themes following prefers-color-scheme).
